Findings.Title: Remove redundant AddOpenApi activation
Findings.Message: Remove 'AddOpenApi()' because Blueprint HTTP hosts now expose OpenAPI by default.
Findings.Description: Legacy Blueprint migrations should remove parameterless AddOpenApi() activation calls because the source-generated HTTP host already implies the OpenAPI surface.

Findings.Title: Migrate configured AddOpenApi activation
Findings.Message: Migrate configured 'AddOpenApi(...)' usage to the future 'ConfigureOpenApi(...)' host-level seam because OpenAPI is no longer activated through BlueprintApiBuilder.
Findings.Description: Legacy Blueprint migrations should treat configured AddOpenApi(...) calls as configuration-required work rather than a safe auto-fix because the customization must move to the future host-level ConfigureOpenApi seam.

Findings.Title: Migrate configured AddAuthentication activation
Findings.Message: Migrate configured 'AddAuthentication(...)' usage through the new authentication configuration path because auth stages are no longer activated through BlueprintApiBuilder feature toggles.
Findings.Description: Legacy Blueprint migrations should treat configured AddAuthentication(...) calls as configuration-required work because context loading and consumer-owned authentication registration still need an explicit migration seam.

Findings.Title: Migrate FromResource usage
Findings.Message: Migrate 'FromResource(...)' usage because auth/resource inheritance must move into Blueprint's source-generated metadata model.
Findings.Description: Legacy Blueprint migrations should treat FromResource(...) usage as consumer-extension rewrite work because the replacement auth/resource model needs explicit source-generated metadata instead of runtime attribute discovery.

Findings.Title: Migrate auth placeholder usage
Findings.Message: Migrate '{Auth:...}' placeholder usage because auth-template expansion must move into Blueprint's source-generated metadata model.
Findings.Description: Legacy '\{Auth:X}' colon syntax is replaced by '\{Auth.X}' dot-notation. Colon now exclusively means fallback, and dot means property path navigation. 'Auth' is treated as a well-known first segment that resolves from the authorization context.
